content: 1. ABC: This mnemonic stands for Airway, Breathing, and Circulation, which are the primary steps in assessing and managing a patient in an emergency situation. 2. APGAR: This is a backronym used to evaluate the health of newborns immediately after birth. It stands for Appearance, Pulse, Grimace, Activity, and Respiration. 3. ASHICE: This mnemonic is used for patient handovers and includes Age, Sex, History, Injuries/Illness, Condition, and ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival) or extra information. 4. FAST: This is a mnemonic for recognizing stroke symptoms: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, and Time to call emergency services. 5. H’s and T’s: These represent the reversible causes of cardiac arrest, such as Hypoxia, Hypovolemia, Hydrogen ion (acidosis), Hypo-/Hyperkalemia, Hypothermia, Tension pneumothorax, Tamponade (cardiac), Toxins, and Thrombosis (pulmonary or coronary). 6. Is Path Warm?: This mnemonic identifies suicide risk factors: Ideation, Substance abuse, Purposelessness, Anxiety, Trapped feelings, Hopelessness, Withdrawal, Anger, Recklessness, and Mood changes. 7. OPQRST: This is a symptom assessment checklist: Onset, Provocation/Palliation, Quality, Region/Radiation, Severity, and Time. 8. RICE: This mnemonic is used for managing sprains and bruises: Rest, Ice, Compression, and Elevation. 9. SOCRATES: This is a structured approach to evaluating pain: Site, Onset, Character, Radiation, Alleviating factors/Associated symptoms, Timing, Exacerbating factors, and Severity. 10. SOAP: This is a method for documenting medical records: Subjective, Objective, Assessment, and Plan. 11. SLUDGE: This mnemonic describes symptoms of cholinergic toxicity: Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, Gastrointestinal upset, and Emesis. 12. Afferent vs. Efferent: Afferent connections arrive at the central nervous system, while efferent connections exit it. 13. Anterior Leg Muscles: The mnemonic The Hospitals Are Not Dirty Places helps recall the structures: Tibialis anterior, Extensor Hallucis longus, Anterior tibial Artery, Deep fibular Nerve, Extensor Digitorum longus, and Peroneus tertius. 14. Brachial Plexus Posterior Cord Branches: Mnemonics like STAR (Subscapular, Thoracodorsal, Axillary, Radial) and RATS (Radial, Axillary, Thoracodorsal, Subscapular) help remember the branches. 15. Lateral Cord Branches: Mnemonics such as Lucy Loves Me or Look My Lancer represent Lateral pectoral nerve, Musculocutaneous nerve, and Lateral root of the Median nerve. 16. Medial Cord Branches: Mnemonics like Most Medical Men Use Morphine or Union of 4 Medials represent Medial pectoral nerve, Medial cutaneous nerve of the arm, Medial cutaneous nerve of the forearm, Ulnar nerve, and Medial root of the Median nerve. 17. 5 Main Nerves of the Brachial Plexus: The mnemonic My Aunty Recognised My Uncle represents Musculocutaneous, Axillary, Radial, Median, and Ulnar nerves. 18. Cavernous Sinus Contents: The mnemonic OTOM CAT helps recall the structures: Oculomotor nerve (III), Trochlear nerve (IV), Ophthalmic nerve (V1), Maxillary nerve (V2), Carotid artery, Abducent nerve (VI), and T (termination of OTOM). 19. Coeliac Trunk Branches: The mnemonic Left Hand Side represents Left gastric artery, Hepatic artery, and Splenic artery. 20. Tarsal Tunnel Contents: The mnemonic Tom, Dick, and Harry (or Tom, Dick, and Very Nervous Harry) represents Tibialis posterior, Flexor Digitorum longus, Flexor Hallucis longus, artery, vein, and nerve. 21. Diaphragmatic Apertures: The mnemonic I ate ten eggs at twelve represents the levels of the diaphragm: Inferior vena cava (T8), Esophagus (T10), and Aorta (T12). 22. Carpal Bones: Mnemonics like Some Lovers Try Positions That They Can’t Handle or She Looks Too Pretty Try To Catch Her represent Scaphoid, Lunate, Triquetrum, Pisiform, Trapezium, Trapezoid, Capitate, and Hamate. 23. Essential Amino Acids: The mnemonic PVT TIM HALL always argues, never tires represents Phenylalanine, Valine, Threonine, Tryptophan, Isoleucine, Methionine, Histidine, Arginine, Leucine, and Lysine. 24. Aortic Regurgitation Causes: The mnemonic CREAM represents Congenital, Rheumatic damage, Endocarditis, Aortic dissection/Aortic root dilation, and Marfan’s syndrome. 25. Aortic Stenosis Symptoms: The mnemonic SAD represents Syncope, Angina, and Dyspnea. 26. Atrial Fibrillation Causes: The mnemonic PIRATES represents Pulmonary causes (e.g., PE, COPD), Iatrogenic, Rheumatic heart disease, Atherosclerotic causes (e.g., MI, CAD), Thyroid (hyperthyroidism), Endocarditis, and Sick sinus syndrome. 27. Beck’s Triad for Cardiac Tamponade: The mnemonic 3 D’s represents Distant heart sounds, Distended jugular veins, and Decreased arterial pressure. 28. CHF Treatment: The mnemonic LMNOP represents Lasix, Morphine, Nitrates, Oxygen, and Vasopressors. 29. MI Management: The mnemonic BOOMAR represents Bed rest, Oxygen, Opiates, Monitor, Anticoagulate, and Reduce clot size. 30. Shock Symptoms: The mnemonic TV SPARC CUBE represents Thirst, Vomiting, Sweating, Pulse weak, Anxious, Respirations shallow/rapid, Cool, Cyanotic, Unconscious, BP low, and Eyes blank. 31. Syncope Causes: The mnemonic HEAD HEART VESSELS categorizes causes into CNS (e.g., Hypoxia, Epilepsy, Anxiety, Dysfunctional brainstem), Cardiac (e.g., Heart attack, Embolism, Aortic obstruction, Rhythm disturbance), and Vascular (e.g., Vasovagal, Ectopic, Situational, Subclavian steal, Low systemic vascular resistance). 32. Pain History Checklist: The mnemonic SOCRATES represents Site, Onset, Character, Radiation, Alleviating factors/Associated symptoms, Timing, Exacerbating factors, and Severity. 33. Abdominal Swelling Causes: The mnemonic 9 F’s represents Fat, Feces, Fluid, Flatus, Fetus, Full-sized tumors, Full bladder, Fibroids, and False pregnancy. 34. Mental State Examination: The mnemonic Assessed Mental State To Be Positively Clinically Unremarkable represents Appearance and behavior, Mood, Speech, Thinking, Behavioral abnormalities, Perception abnormalities, Cognition, and Understanding of condition. This format ensures clarity and precision, making it suitable for medical professionals.
